name: Haman's 10 Sons
title: The Sons of Israel's Enemy
summary: Haman's ten sons were descendants of Agagite Haman, the enemy of the Jews in Persia. They were killed along with other enemies of the Jews on the day appointed for the destruction of the Jewish people, and their bodies were hung up as a public sign of God's protection of His people.

keyEvents.title: The Names of Haman's Sons
keyEvents.description: The Bible lists the names of all ten sons: Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha.

keyEvents.title: Killed by the Jews in Susa
keyEvents.description: On the thirteenth day of the month of Adar, Haman's ten sons were killed by the Jews in the fortress of Susa, along with 500 other enemies.

keyEvents.title: The Jews Took No Spoil
keyEvents.description: Although the Jews had the right to take spoil from their enemies, including Haman's sons, they did not lay hands on the plunder—a sign that this was self-defense, not greed.

keyEvents.title: Bodies Hung Up Publicly
keyEvents.description: At Esther's request, King Ahasuerus ordered that the bodies of Haman's ten sons be hanged on poles in Susa as a public warning.

keyEvents.title: Part of the Purim celebration
keyEvents.description: The killing of Haman's sons and the victory over the enemies of the Jews became the basis for the annual festival of Purim, where the Jews celebrate their deliverance.
